title: Call: Sonoran Cold Freight Dispatch — Trailer SCF-53817 at Tucson

callee.name: Carla Estrada
callee.label: Director of Logistics, Pinecrest Fresh Cut

transcript.speaker: SONORAN DISPATCH
transcript.text: Morning, this is Marisol at Sonoran Cold Freight dispatch. I'm calling about your load on truck 2219, trailer SCF-53817. That's 1,320 cases of your chopped romaine headed for your Dallas DC.

transcript.speaker: SONORAN DISPATCH
transcript.text: He's fueling at the Pilot near Tucson, eastbound on I-10. The reefer reads 36 degrees, so the product's fine. My driver has 6 hours and 40 minutes left on his clock. Your Dallas people said something about a hold, but nobody's sent me anything, so as of now he's still dispatched to Dallas.

transcript.speaker: SONORAN DISPATCH
transcript.text: So here's what I can do. One, I turn him around to your Phoenix DC, which is about 2 hours west, and he's there before lunch. Two, I park him at a cold yard here in Tucson, but that's $185 a day detention plus fuel to keep the reefer running, and I need a ship-to and a release from you before he goes anywhere after that. If I don't hear from you by 08:45, he keeps going to Dallas. And I'll need it in writing, email or a change in your TMS, not just a phone call.

transcript.speaker: DALLAS DC
transcript.text: Logistics, it's Terrence Boyd at Dallas, I'm cutting in on your line because you're not picking up texts. Cornerstone just called. They say the 2,100 cases we sent out since 04:00 are sitting in back rooms and on shelves at 38 stores, and they want us to go pull it, not them.

transcript.speaker: DALLAS DC
transcript.text: I've got 9 people on the floor. I can either send them out to pull 38 stores, or keep them here and count the 3,000 by 10:30. Not both. Tell me which one.

transcript.speaker: LOGISTICS
transcript.text: Marisol, Terrence Boyd, here's the call.

transcript.speaker: SONORAN DISPATCH
transcript.text: Okay. Send me the email at dispatch so I've got it on file, and I'll call him at the pump. Clock's running.

voiceStyles.SONORAN DISPATCH: Woman in her 40s, brisk, practical trucking dispatcher, phones ringing behind her
voiceStyles.DALLAS DC: Man in his 50s, Texas accent, tired and short on patience, warehouse forklift beeps behind him
voiceStyles.LOGISTICS: Played live by the Director of Logistics

instructorNote: This tests the Stop the Truck decision and how LOG uses its people. Look for LOG to stop SCF-53817 before 08:45, either by sending it to quarantine at the Phoenix DC (34–38°F) or by holding it at the cold yard, and to confirm that in writing or in the TMS (PPHTRP 4.1). LOG should keep the Dallas crew on the physical count of the 3,000 to meet the 4-hour target and set up store pulls through Cornerstone store teams or temporary crews, with pulled cases counted by lot code.
